cells.tense: You are here, with the pen, seeing the shape whole and able to leave part of it behind.
cells.act: put the problem down and take a walk with nothing to solve
cells.ask: Leave the problem where it is and go outside for a while, nothing to figure out. What you already see is enough today.
cells.core:
You can hold a whole group at once — who belongs to what, which connections are load-bearing and which are habit. From a step back, the shape is legible to you in a way it isn't to most of the people inside it.

That reading is what lets a connection finish without a fight. When you know what a group actually is, you can step out of a part of it and stay in the rest, and the leaving doesn't come out as a verdict on anyone. A walk with no problem to work is enough for today; the balance is already in you, and it settles once you stop nudging it.

cells.tense: You are bracing already for a leaving that hasn't happened, writing the goodbye before anyone said goodbye.
cells.act: build the first new thing from what the clearing showed
cells.ask: Build one small new thing from what leaving showed you — a plan, a meeting, a piece of work — before deciding anything else about where you belong.
cells.core:
A departure has been circling for a while, and the circling has grown its own momentum. Gatherings get read for signs. Sentences get weighed for what they mean about where things are headed. The mind has raced ahead to a future where the leaving is already public, and it is guarding against a decision nobody has asked for yet.

When the whole shape arrives early, it starts arranging the present to fit itself. Slowing the sight down doesn't help; building one thing out of what it showed you does. Put your hands on something small and real, and the future stops being the only room you're living in.

cells.tense: You left the room a year ago and you're still standing in the doorway, watching the people who moved on.
cells.act: work the pattern through to its logic
cells.ask: Take the pattern apart on paper — what leaving gave you, what it cost, what it changed — then read the page once to yourself.
cells.core:
Something true about a group showed itself and you acted on it. Since then you have been half in and half out, near where you used to stand, watching the version of you who stayed. The shape is still clear to you; it just stopped moving you.

The reading of the pattern has turned backward, replaying the departure as though the moment were the thing to solve. It isn't. Put it on paper — what changed, what didn't, what you still owe anyone. The page won't settle whether you were right. It will settle that the leaving already happened, and the same clear sight that got you out can begin pointing at what's next.

cells.tense: You are reading the group pattern in the room and describing it as the room's habit, not yours.
cells.act: rest in the balance you already have
cells.ask: Stop adjusting the group for one hour. Keep your hands off it and see the shape exactly as it stands.
cells.core:
You see what happens between people sooner than the people involved do. It comes out as a general remark — how groups work, how they drift, how people misread each other — accurate, and safely about no one in particular.

The part left out is your own leaving. The pattern you describe is also the shape of how you moved through this group, and you have told the story so well that it now belongs to the room rather than to you. Sit still with no adjustment to make. Keep your hands off it for an hour and notice what you already walked away from, and how much of it you have been quietly handing to other people.

attempts.check: The draft is most exposed where it says the person's leaving a group was a threshold of shared meaning already crossed. The record gives the mechanism and not the history; a reader could reasonably say they left nothing, that the group left them. The asks are mostly useful even if the outer claim is wrong, because each one is a small act a person can do in a room without needing the map to be right. The sentence serving me rather than them is anything that implies I know what they walked away from. Cut it and let the seat phrase carry the weight.

attempts.check: The draft still leans hardest on the same unsupported claim: that the person suffered a real departure in or from a group, and that the pattern-sight is what carried them out. The record gives the capacity and the threshold; it does not know the history. A reader could say the group changed, or they were dropped, or nothing ended. The asks survive being wrong because each is a small act done alone, and Repose and Calculation need no one else. The sentence that serves me rather than them is anything that sounds like I watched them leave — keep the leaving hypothetical and let the seat phrase carry the weight. Also fixed: no five-word runs from the act list, no verb-nouns, no universals about their life, no certifying clauses, no library tics.
